{'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'thinking', 'thinking': 'OK, now I understand the bug. Inside `handleReplayTimeout`:\n\n```ts\nhandleReplayTimeout = async () => {\n    const { replayTimeout } = this.props\n\n    const { mode, replay, wellStateId } = this.state\n\n    let nextReplayTimeoutId\n\n    if (mode === \'REPLAYING\') {\n      await this.handleRedo()\n\n      if (wellStateId + 1 in replay) {\n        nextReplayTimeoutId = setTimeout(this.handleReplayTimeout, replayTimeout)\n      }\n    } else {\n      console.warn(\'Ignoring input replay step because mode is\', mode)\n    }\n\n    this.setState({\n      replayTimeoutId: nextReplayTimeoutId\n    })\n  }\n```\n\nWhen the replay runs out of inputs:\n1. `handleRedo` performs the last move. Note: `handleMove` updates state. If the last move is a "D" (down) that doesn\'t end the game, mode stays \'REPLAYING\'.\n2. `wellStateId + 1 in replay` is false (replay has no more entries), so no new timeout is scheduled.\n3. `setState({ replayTimeoutId: undefined })`.\n4. But `mode` stays \'REPLAYING\' forever! The render shows "replaying..." and there are no controls. The user is stuck.\n\nWait, actually there\'s a subtle race condition here: `await this.handleRedo()` calls `handleMove`, which calls `this.setState(await this.logic.handleMove(...))`. In React 18/19 with automatic batching, does `this.state` inside `handleReplayTimeout` after the `await` reflect the new state? Let me think. `this.setState` triggers a re-render; in React 19 (concurrent), updates inside async handlers may be processed... Actually with class components, `setState` is asynchronous, but React flushes updates. After `await this.handleRedo()`, control returns to the continuation of `handleReplayTimeout`. Has React committed the state update at that point?\n\n`handleRedo` is async: `await this.handleMove(replay[wellStateId])`. `handleMove` is async: `this.setState(await this.logic.handleMove(this.state, move))`. `logic.handleMove` is probably async (awaits AI). So after the `await`, `this.setState` is called. React\'s setState on a class component outside an event handler is... In React 18+, all setState calls are batched and processed in a microtask-ish way (actually scheduled, then processed). Hmm.\n\nThe key question for the bug: when `handleReplayTimeout` runs after `await this.handleRedo()`, what is `this.state.mode`?\n\nWait, actually `handleReplayTimeout` reads `this.state` at the start, before the `await`. So `mode`, `replay`, `wellStateId` are the values at the time the timeout fired. Then `handleRedo` executes the move for index `wellStateId`. (\r\n            yActual >= bar &&\r\n            nextWell[yActual + row] === (1 << wellWidth) - 1\r\n          ) {\r\n            // move all lines above this point down\r\n            for (let k = yActual + row; k > 1; k--) {\r\n              nextWell[k] = nextWell[k - 1]\r\n            }\r\n\r\n            // insert a new blank line at the top\r\n            // though of course the top line will always be blank anyway\r\n            nextWell[0] = 0\r\n\r\n            nextScore++\r\n          }\r\n        }\r\n        nextPiece = null\r\n      } else {\r\n        // No move\r\n        nextPiece = piece\r\n      }\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    return {\r\n      core: {\r\n        well: nextWell,\r\n        score: nextScore\r\n      },\r\n      ai: nextAiState,\r\n      piece: nextPiece\r\n better add that to the list\r\n          // do NOT check locations, they aren\'t significant here\r\n          possibleFutures.push(nextState.core)\r\n        } else {\r\n          // transform succeeded?\r\n          // new location? aiResult\r\n      : [aiResult, aiState]\r\n\r\n    if (pieceIds.includes(unsafePieceId)) {\r\n      return [unsafePieceId, nextAiState]\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    throw Error(`Bad piece ID: ${unsafePieceId}`)\r\n  }\r\n\r\n  const getFirstWellState = async ({ enemy }: GameState): Promise<WellState> => {\r\n    const firstCoreState = {\r\n      well: Array(wellDepth).fill(0),\r\n      score: 0\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    const [firstPieceId, firstAiState] = await validateAiResult(enemy, firstCoreState, undefined)\r\n\r\n    return {\r\n      core: firstCoreState,\r\n      ai: firstAiState,\r\n      piece: rotationSystem.placeNewPiece(wellWidth, firstPieceId)\r\n    }\r\n  }\r\n\r\n  /**\r\n    Accepts the input of a move and attempts to apply that\r\n    transform to the live piece in the live well.\r\n    Returns the new state.
